solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scholar crams it almost all ingeniously into novel

indicators.note: worked over ingeniously, these letters are cleverly rearranged into something new
almost all of the word all is kept, cut back to its opening letter

explanation.surface: A student stuffs nearly everything cleverly into the book they are writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the word all to A; SCHOLAR, CRAMS, IT and that A are shuffled, 'ingeniously' signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's festive ghost story of 1843 is a famous novella, here simply called a novel.

clue.text: Rainy spells bringing forth flowers in May proverbially

definitions.text: Rainy spells bringing forth flowers in May proverbially

parts.words: Rainy spells bringing forth flowers in May proverbially
parts.note: the proverb says the brief rain of the month before May brings May flowers

explanation.surface: Wet weather that, the proverb says, produces May blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring rain bursts of the fourth month are what the old rhyme credits with making May blooms grow.

clue.text: In Latin this edition of the Bible brings chaos

indicators.note: in puts the Bible edition inside the Latin word

parts.note: hoc is Latin for this
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A particular Latin Bible causes disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it belongs with 'Latin', but it is the container signal; AV, the Authorised Version, is the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread destruction and disorder is a straightforward synonym for chaos.

clue.text: Lack of education in English can go right if corrected

indicators.note: if corrected means the letters, set right, take a new order

parts.note: the word in kept as written, followed by E, the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: In English lessons, things can turn out fine if errors are fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if corrected' rearranges IN, E (English), CAN, GO and R (right). 'Lack of education' reads as the topic of the sentence, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unschooled and uninformed is the state of not knowing, a near synonym.

clue.text: Small piece of mosaic being inserted into mobile art

indicators.note: inserted into places the Latin word inside the shuffled letters
mobile means moving, so the letters move around

parts.note: esse is Latin for being, existence

explanation.surface: A tile of mosaic is set into a mobile sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' gives the anagram TRA, and 'inserted into' puts the Latin infinitive for being inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tile or small block of stone or glass used in a mosaic is the technical term.

clue.text: Dirigible looks trendy

parts.note: airs are manners or looks, as in putting on airs
hip means trendy

explanation.surface: A blimp appears fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible is a steerable lighter-than-air craft, such as a zeppelin.

clue.text: Frank film director's salute to origins of realistic acting

parts.note: to cap is to touch one's cap in salute

indicators.note: origins of picks the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: An honest director pays tribute to the roots of naturalistic performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like the adjective honest, but it is the director's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Capra directed It's a Wonderful Life, a well-known Hollywood filmmaker.

clue.text: Repeat new ariette about the Queen

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the royal pair
new means the letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A singer is asked to perform a fresh little aria about the monarch again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ARIETTE into REITATE, which goes 'about' ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do something again is a direct synonym of repeat.

clue.text: Black bird's prey

definitions.meaning: glossy jet black, as of hair
as a verb, to plunder or devour greedily

explanation.surface: A dark-feathered bird is someone's victim.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for jet black, as the crow-like bird, and as an old verb meaning to plunder or devour.

clue.text: Around start of holidays imps are transformed into perfect angels

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the single letter, enclosing it
being transformed, the letters change into a new arrangement
the start of holidays is its first letter

explanation.surface: Mischievous little devils turn into angels once the holidays begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like the verb, but it is part of the fodder; 'transformed' makes SERAPIM, which goes 'Around' the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphs are the highest order of angels in Christian tradition, so a fitting plural for flawless heavenly beings.

clue.text: Travel league to lair and plunder Argonauts' target

parts.note: to go is to travel
a den is an animal's lair
to fleece is to rob or plunder

explanation.surface: Instructions for a raiding trip: journey to the hideout and loot it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason and his crew on the Argo sailed to Colchis to seize this mythical ram's coat of gold.

clue.text: City and lake in clover?

definitions.meaning: a Swiss city standing on a lake of the same name
alfalfa, a cloverlike fodder plant; the question mark admits it is only a relative of clover

explanation.surface: Asks whether a city by a lake is living in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in clover' looks like the idiom for living comfortably, but clover just points to the fodder plant alfalfa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss city on its own lake, and also the British name for alfalfa, a leguminous forage crop much like clover.

clue.text: Happiness cut short by house's rejection

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: heaven is a state of bliss or happiness
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Someone's joy ends abruptly when a household turns them away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last letter off HEAVEN; 'by' just joins it to HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the heave-ho is an idiom for dismissing or throwing them out.

clue.text: Virile sort of chief, shunning public notice

indicators.note: shunning means the notice is avoided, taken out of the word

parts.note: a headman is a tribal or village chief
an ad is an advertisement, a public notice

explanation.surface: A manly kind of leader avoids publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongly built, macho man is informally called this, a type of muscular masculinity.

clue.text: Criminal mafia men run powerful computer

indicators.note: criminal suggests these letters are bent out of shape

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Gangsters operate a high-powered computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large central computer serving many users is the classic high-capacity machine.

clue.text: Destroyed padre's name almost & character

indicators.note: destroyed letters are broken up and rebuilt in a fresh order
almost all of name is kept, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A priest's reputation is almost wrecked by some symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NAME to NAM, and 'Destroyed' shuffles PADRES with NAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol & is the typographic sign for 'and', called by that name.

clue.text: Capone, for one, causing uproar always

parts.note: a racket is a din, an uproar
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A gangster forever makes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was a notorious gangster who ran illegal businesses, an example of the type.

clue.text: Fish pasty temptation

parts.note: pasty as an adjective means pale-faced, white
bait is a lure or temptation

explanation.surface: A savoury pastry is offered as a lure to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the Cornish pie, but it is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Small young herring and sprats eaten whole and fried are a type of fish dish.

clue.text: Hail storm's prevailing

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A hailstorm is dominating the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail storm' reads as weather, but splits into a greeting and a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical, usual or common, as in the prevailing or average view, a loose adjective synonym.

clue.text: Absolutely worst person possible is ridiculously pettish

indicators.note: ridiculously means the letters are absurdly scrambled

explanation.surface: The most awful individual imaginable is absurdly petulant.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for the very worst, used of a person or thing that is utterly dreadful.

clue.text: Initially char leaves everything as new

definitions.text: Initially char leaves everything as new

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady leaves the house spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning lady; the first letters of the clue's five words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes her result.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotless, freshly scrubbed home looks as good as new, which is what a cleaner achieves.

clue.text: Judge delayed raise expenditure

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A judge has been slow to approve higher spending.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost an economy by increasing government spending or money supply is an economics term.

clue.text: Quickly stripping away top three parts of shell

indicators.text: stripping away top three parts of
indicators.note: removing the top three letters of the word for shell, the opening ones in a down light

parts.note: a carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise or crab

explanation.surface: Peeling off the upper layers of a shell fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at speed, swiftly, is an old-fashioned adverb sense.

clue.text: Closely examine torn label after end of the year

indicators.note: after places the shuffled label at the end
the end of the word the is its final letter
torn means the word label is ripped apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises a ripped label at the close of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of the year' looks like one phrase meaning December, but splits into the last letter of 'the' plus Y; 'torn' gives EBALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare hard at something, scrutinising it face to face, is an informal verb sense.

clue.text: American soldier rises to meet old friend

indicators.note: rises in a down light means the word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US serviceman stands to greet an old pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a pal, borrowed into English for a mate.

clue.text: At sea Maria, going aft, caught a large squid

indicators.note: going aft means the jumbled name goes to the back

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the name's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor called Maria, moving to the stern, landed a big squid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' jumbles MARIA into AMARI, which goes behind C, A and L ('going aft').
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian word for squid is used on menus for squid rings, usually fried.

clue.text: The Spanish fish is cut off

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A Spanish fish has been severed.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit a sound or syllable in speech is to drop or cut it off.

clue.text: Sober geezer once reformed as protagonist in 1A

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A man who has sobered up is described as reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' is apt: Dickens's miser does reform at the end of the book.
explanation.definitionFit: The miserly hero of Dickens's ghost story, visited by spirits on Christmas Eve, is its main character.
